Capitalise on customer testimonials If your customers write positive things about you online, why not shout about it? Repurposing testimonials as social media posts is the best way to increase loyalty, but also to populate your content calendar with evergreen content. That's right—testimonials don't have an expiration date, so you can easily repurpose them whenever you run out of fresh ideas for posting on your social media channels. The final post doesn't have to be overly complicated in terms of design —it could be as easy as repurposing a tweet and adding your brand colours to a template you create in Canva . Then, you're good to go! Best channels to share this content type: Instagram, X, Facebook, LinkedIn, Google My Business. 6. Jump onto trending memes This type of fun content often arises from news and current events and can get your brand exposure and engagement if you can strike while the iron is hot. Use trending words and pair them with a fun meme. Add a niched comment to ensure you're targeting the right audience while staying on brand. Memes are a great way to increase engagement and reach because they are relatable. Plus, they offer your brand to show a more relaxed, fun side. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sendible (@sendible) Best channels to share this content type: X, Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook 7. Provide self-care and well-being tips People are burnt out from too much screen time, mental health has taken a hit, and social media is partly to blame. Spending too much time on social media isn't good for anyone, and has been shown to increase anxiety, depression, and other issues. Social media usage is at an all-time high, with the average user spending 2 hours and 30 minutes dail y on social media. So, offering your followers some self-care tips and success stories can go a long way. Why not show your followers some compassion by posting weekly about ways that they can take care of themselves better, or even encouraging them to switch off from social and reconnect with the real world - they might thank you for it. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sendible (@sendible) Best channels to share this content type: X, Instagram, LinkedIn 8. Share original research and data on your social media platforms If you work in an industry that deals with data and carries out regular research, why not repurpose your findings visually, easily digestibly for your followers? Charts and statistics work brilliantly on Instagram because there are so many unique ways to present them on Instagram Stories or as in-feed posts. Best channels to share this content type: Facebook, LinkedIn, X, Instagram, Pinterest 9. Create short-form videos Don't have time to create long-form videos? You're in luck, because short-form videos are the most popular social media content. But saying you should create them is not enough. So here are some actionable ideas: Hop on trending audio and add niched captions. This type of video is great for increasing your reach. Add video memes to your image. Just like image memes, this type of video post tends to perform well because it's relatable. Record yourself showing to the left and right, then add overlay text to create a "this or that" video. This is a great way to boost the number of comments. Film yourself while doing a daily activity, then add a list of steps to achieve the goal. This will cause viewers to pause your video to read the list, increasing engagement and watch time. View this post on Instagram A post shared by The North Face (@thenorthface) The best channels to share this content type are Instagram Reels, Facebook Reels, Tiktok, and YouTube Shorts. 10. Ask your followers questions Sometimes, marketers forget that social media isn't just a distribution channel. Your followers don't want to be given the hard sell with endless product posts - they want to be heard. So, why not spend some time getting to know them by asking questions and encouraging them to engage? Depending on the type and amount of engagement you receive from this style of post, you could repurpose your followers' answers into further posts. Best channels to share this content type: X, Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn 11. Utilise user-generated content User-generated content is essentially content that's already been created for you by your biggest fans - talk about convenience! Not only does user-generated content save you time on the content creation side, but it's also a great tool for adding a sense of authenticity to your brand, so it can be quite an effective part of your content strategy. To cultivate this sort of user-generated content, create a hashtag and encourage your customers to use it whenever they post about your brand on their social media platforms. You don't need to dress these posts up or add any special effects, the more stripped down and real they are, the better. Just make sure you ask permission to share the content by reaching out and asking to repost it on your accounts. Ultimately, there isn't anything much more powerful for a brand than social proof showing real people using (and enjoying) your product or service, as Estrid shows: Best channels to share this content type: Instagram, X, Facebook, LinkedIn, Pinterest 12. Get creative with emojis Using emojis helps to humanise your brand and studies show that 44% of consumers are more likely to purchase products that are advertised using emojis. And let's face it - emojis are fun! You can use them to inspire people to vote in the comments or by adding a "like" in the form of the emoji. Also, remember that emoji usage should be relevant and appropriate to your message - you don't want to come off as insensitive for pairing an emoji with a serious or sensitive post. Since your audience is primed for it, why not share articles about developments in your industry for your followers to read or video clips of news events that are happening? Do make sure to always check your sources before you share - fake news is prolific and could discredit your brand. Best channels to share this content type: X, LinkedIn, Facebook 16. Share product news and releases Keeping followers updated with your brand's movements and teasing them with new releases and developments is a great way to grab their attention and get them excited about your offering. If you're planning to release a new feature, maximise the opportunity from a content perspective by counting down to d-day with in-feed posts. Best channels to share this content type: X, LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram 17. Share product photos Product photos are a brand's bread and butter on social media. They're also a frequently used type of visual content for social media marketing campaigns. Beautifully crafted shots can really help to solidify your brand's aesthetic, and who doesn't love a pretty picture?! Couple your striking product photo with a strong caption and you're onto a winner! Best channels to share this content type: X, LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, Pinterest, TikTok 18. Just ensure that you make the terms and conditions clear to participants before they enter, to avoid any disappointment or confusion. Best channels to share this content type: LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, Pinterest 19. text: The most useful social media content ideas are tied to a job: teaching your audience something, showing how you work, proving you deliver, starting a conversation, or selling. Pick ideas by goal, match each to the format its platform rewards, and schedule them as a balanced weekly mix. The 75 ideas below are grouped that way. Most idea lists stop at the list. The hard part is not finding an idea; it is choosing the right one for this Tuesday's slot, in the right format for each network, and doing it again next week. So each idea below comes with the networks and formats that suit it, based on what the platforms and the largest public studies say they reward in 2026. After the lists you will find the best idea types per network, quick starters for six industries, an effort guide, a step-by-step method to turn ideas into a month of scheduled posts, and a worked example. Key findings Format choice changes results more than topic choice on some networks. In Buffer's analysis of more than 45 million posts, LinkedIn carousels had a 21.77% median engagement rate against 7.35% for video, and Instagram carousels 6.9% against 4.4% for single images ( Buffer, March 2026 ). Sends and saves are ranking signals. Instagram's Feed ranking predicts how likely you are to send a post in a direct message and to swipe through all of a carousel ( Meta Transparency Center ). Ideas worth passing on travel further. Replies pay. Buffer's study of nearly 2 million posts linked replying to comments with up to 42% higher engagement on Threads and about 30% on LinkedIn ( Buffer ). Conversation ideas only work if you answer. Trends expire fast. 27% of consumers think trend participation is only effective within 24 to 48 hours of a trend's lifespan, and a third find brands jumping on viral trends "embarrassing" ( Sprout Social Index 2025 , 4,044 consumers). Original ideas are now rewarded directly. Instagram limits recommendations for accounts that mostly post unoriginal photos, carousels and Reels ( Instagram, April 2026 ). Consistency matters more than any single idea. Creators who posted in 20 or more weeks out of 26 got about 450% more engagement per post than those who posted in four weeks or fewer, across more than 100,000 Buffer users ( Buffer ). What's changed in 2026 A few platform changes this year shift which ideas are worth your time. Originality is a ranking rule Instagram's April 2026 update says adding "a border, watermark, subtitles or a credit in the captions" does not make reposted content original, and that accounts that mostly post unoriginal content lose eligibility for recommendations ( Instagram ). Facebook made a similar change in March 2026. Ideas that document your own work, customers and opinions are now safer bets than curated reposts. LinkedIn added collaborative posts and cracked down on generic content In July 2026, LinkedIn launched collaborative posts, which let members and Company Pages "post jointly with up to five other members or via Company Pages" ( LinkedIn ). In September, it said it limits the distribution of "AI slop", content that is "generic, repetitive, recycled", and reported a 40% drop in views for posts classed that way ( LinkedIn ). Partner posts and opinionated, specific posts are in; generic tips are out. Threads became a bigger network with communities Meta said in June 2026 that "Threads has reached 500 million monthly active users", and added a Communities Hub and topic controls ( Meta ). Conversation ideas, the Join section below, have a larger home than they did a year ago. Testing ideas got easier Instagram's trial reels are "shown to non-followers first", with views, likes, comments and shares visible after about 24 hours, so you can test an idea before your followers see it ( Instagram ). That makes riskier ideas, such as an unpopular opinion or a new series format, cheaper to try. How to use this list Use these ideas with content pillars. If your pillars are "Teach", "Show", "Prove", "Join" and "Sell", pick a few ideas from each section, assign them to calendar slots, and you have a balanced week without wondering what to post each morning. Our guide to creating a social media strategy explains how to set pillars, and our guide to organising content ideas shows how to keep an idea bank. These notes match idea types to what each platform rewards. Instagram Teach carousels and Show videos. Carousels led Instagram engagement at 6.9% of reach in Buffer's data, and Instagram's Feed ranking predicts carousel completion and DM sends. Instagram also advises using "relevant keywords in your content, your caption, your bio and your hashtags" for search ( Instagram ). TikTok Quick tips, myth versus fact, processes and rankings. TikTok weighs user interactions most and says follower count is not a direct factor ( TikTok ), so a strong idea from a small account can travel. LinkedIn Lessons, opinions, numbers and customer stories. LinkedIn says "images typically result in a 2x higher comment rate" and companies that post weekly "see a 2x lift in engagement" ( LinkedIn ). Our LinkedIn content strategy guide has a weekly plan. Then add your specific detail, because the detail is what makes an idea yours. A content calendar with pillars already assigned to each slot turns this into a two-minute decision. Save involved ideas, especially video, for a batching day. A useful habit is to film three or four involved ideas in one session each month, then fill the weeks between with quick and medium ideas, so your cadence never depends on finding a free afternoon. How to execute any idea well An idea is only as good as its first second. These rules apply to every idea on the list. Open with the payoff Instagram's Reels ranking predicts "how likely you are to watch less than three seconds of a reel" ( Meta Transparency Center ). Whatever the format, lead with the result, the surprising number or the mistake, not with a greeting or a logo. On text networks, the first line does the same job. Keep video short enough to finish Instagram says that "in order to be recommended", reels "must be 3 minutes or less" ( Instagram ). Most quick-tip and process ideas work best well under a minute, which makes completion more likely. Give people a reason to save or send A checklist, a template, a comparison or a number someone will want later earns saves; something funny, useful or surprising earns sends. Both are named predictions in Instagram's ranking. Ask yourself, before you schedule: who would send this, and to whom? Post often enough for ideas to compound Buffer's 2026 analysis of more than 52 million posts found that top-performing accounts post more often than the median account, and do so consistently across the year, and that accounts which skipped a week underperformed their own baseline ( Buffer ). A good idea posted once is a post; a good idea turned into a weekly series is a reason to follow. Reply while the post is new Conversation ideas depend on you answering. Set a reply window for the first hour after your most important posts go out, and treat the best replies as material for the next post (idea 54). How to turn ideas into a month of scheduled posts: an 8-step method Set your pillars and networks. Three to five pillars, two to four networks. Choose a cadence you can keep. Our guide to how often to post gives ranges per network. Build a calendar grid. Assign each slot a pillar, so Monday is Teach and Friday is Join, for example. Our content calendar templates give you a starting grid. Fill slots from the lists above. Pick ideas by pillar, effort and freshness. Add your specific detail. The mistake you actually see, the number you actually have, the customer who agreed to be featured. Write once, adapt per network. One core post, then a version per network. Our guide to repurposing content shows how one idea becomes five posts. Batch and schedule. Write and schedule the month in one or two sessions. See batch content creation . Review monthly. Keep the ideas that earned saves, sends and replies, and retire the rest. In Postprism, steps 6 and 7 happen in one place.
